focus.label: Deponent verbs
focus.blurb: Verbs that look passive but mean something active — watch especially the commands ending in -re and -minī.

focus.label: Gerund
focus.blurb: The verb turned into a noun for 'doing' something: -ndum after ad for purpose, -ndī with a noun, -ndō for 'by doing'.

title: Mīnōs · Corōnis · Fabellae LXIII–LXV
reading: Fabulae Syrae cap. XXVII, 1 · Fabulae Syrae cap. XXVII, 5 · Fabellae Latinae 63–65

focus.label: Present subjunctive · supine
focus.blurb: After ut or nē a verb in the present subjunctive tells what someone wants done; the supine (-um, -ū) names the purpose of going or the respect in which something is so.

focus.label: Present subjunctive
focus.blurb: The present subjunctive's forms (-e- for the 1st conjugation, -a- for the rest) and the ut/nē clauses that use them for wishes, commands and purposes.

title: Coriolānus · Nausicaa · Fabellae LXVI–LXVIII
reading: Fabulae Syrae, Coriolanus (end) · Fabulae Syrae cap. XXVIII, 3 · Fabellae Latinae 66–68

focus.label: Imperfect subjunctive
focus.blurb: When the main verb is past, the subjunctive after ut/nē goes into the imperfect: for results, purposes, commands and questions reported inside the story.

focus.label: Imperfect subjunctive · sequence of tenses
focus.blurb: A past main verb pulls the subjunctive in its clause into the imperfect — the tense of the subjunctive follows the tense of the verb that introduces it.

focus.label: ut/nē clauses · deliberative · cum
focus.blurb: The same ut can report a command, state a purpose or describe a result; the subjunctive alone can ask 'what am I to do?'; and cum with the subjunctive sets the scene ('when/since').

focus.label: Future perfect
focus.blurb: 'Will have done': the tense Latin uses after sī, cum and antequam for something that must be finished before the main future event.

focus.label: Gerundive · passive periphrastic · dative of agent
focus.blurb: The -ndus adjective says something 'must be done', and the person who must do it goes into the dative instead of ā/ab with the ablative.

title: Arachnē · Fabellae LXIX–LXXIV
reading: Fabulae Syrae cap. XXXII, 2 · Fabellae Latinae 69–74

focus.label: Perfect subjunctive
focus.blurb: Used for 'don't' commands (nē + perfect subjunctive) and for questions reported after a present main verb about something already done.

focus.label: Perfect subjunctive · utinam
focus.blurb: More perfect subjunctives, plus utinam ('if only!') for wishes — present subjunctive for a wish that can still come true, imperfect for one that cannot.

focus.label: Pluperfect subjunctive · future imperative
focus.blurb: 'If X had happened, Y would have happened' and 'if only it had…' use the pluperfect subjunctive; the future imperative (-tō, -tōte) gives orders for later.

focus.label: Poetry: elegiac couplet, hendecasyllable · dummodo · dative verbs
focus.blurb: First verse: a long line paired with a shorter one (the elegiac couplet) and Catullus' eleven-syllable line; dummodo ('provided that') takes the subjunctive, and some verbs take a dative object.

focus.label: Poetry: prosody, elision, scansion · Martial
focus.blurb: How to hear a line: long and short syllables, a final vowel swallowed before the next word (elision), and marking the feet — practised on Martial's short, pointed epigrams.
